text: For a smallholder farmer in Preah Vihear, basic pig care requires a nutritionally balanced diet (pigs are monogastric and cannot rely mainly on fibrous forage), reliable clean water, appropriate housing, heat management, and daily observation. Requirements differ substantially by stage — piglets, growing/fattening pigs, pregnant sows, lactating sows, and breeding boars should not automatically receive the same ration. Local feed ingredients can supplement commercial feed but availability does not mean nutritional completeness or safety; feed should be fresh, protected from moisture, and free of mold/chemical contamination. During the wet season (roughly May–October), keeping pig housing dry, well-drained, and clean is critical — standing water and mud increase hygiene problems. During the dry season (roughly November–April), heat is a major stressor since pigs have limited ability to sweat; shade, airflow, adequate water, and practical cooling are important. Daily observation should cover appetite, water intake, growth, manure, breathing, skin, lameness, and behavior. Piglets need particular attention to warmth, nutrition, competition, and risk of being crushed by the sow. Simple pens and locally available feed are realistic for smallholders — intensive-farm recommendations should be adapted, not presented as mandatory. There is not enough province-specific evidence to name a predominant pig breed in Preah Vihear — record the farmer's actual type if known. Exact feed formulations, supplements, and any medication/vaccine dosage should come from a qualified veterinarian, animal-nutrition professional, or registered product label — never generated as universal numbers.
